name: Community Radio Studio
description: A functional radio broadcast facility equipped with old consoles, a battered mixer, emergency power systems, and a skylight. The studio contains broadcasting equipment including an ON AIR sign, microphone, cassette cue system, and tape reels. Windows are present and subject to weather exposure.
physical_traits: ON AIR sign (flickering/unreliable initially, then steady)
Chairs suitable for hanging wet coats
Vending machine in adjacent band room
scene_presence: Aria (threading tape, operating switches, pinning maps, managing broadcast)
Noah (operating mixer, labeling notebook, cueing cassettes)
June (covering whiteboard with road closures and shelter names, operating microphone, creating signage)
Kell (carrying portable antenna, lantern, and tool bag; delivering bread)
narrative_significance: The Community Radio Studio serves as the operational hub for emergency broadcast communications during a crisis event. It functions as a lifeline for the community, coordinating information about road closures, shelter locations, and missing persons. The studio represents resilience and community coordination, operating under emergency power conditions and serving as a gathering place for coordinated relief efforts.
